title: Exploring Our Neighbourhood
seo_title: Exploring Our Neighbourhood Class 4 EVS Worksheet (NCERT Our Wondrous World Ch 2)
standard_code: Class 4, Our Wondrous World Chapter 2: Exploring Our Neighbourhood
standard_text: Places in our neighbourhood; reading simple maps, symbols and the key; directions north, south, east and west; means of transport on land, water and air; road signs and road safety (summary of NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 2).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 4 EVS worksheets for NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 2: places in the neighbourhood, maps and symbols, directions, means of transport and road safety. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Maps and directions help us find our way.
key_sub: The Sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
body_html:
How to think about it

A map is a drawing of a place as seen from above. It uses symbols and colours, explained in its key: blue for water, green for forests and parks, and lines for roads and railways. The four main directions are north, south, east and west; the Sun rises in the east and a compass needle points north.

We travel by land (bus, train, bicycle), water (boat, ship) and air (aeroplane, helicopter). Road signs keep us safe: red means stop, green means go and a zebra crossing is the safe place to cross the road.

Example

The park is north of the school. The school is…

opposite direction

Answer: south of the park

Example

A ferry is…

it carries people across water

Answer: water transport

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up east and west.
  • Crossing the road anywhere.
  • Thinking a map shows things from the side.

faq.q: What does the key of a map tell us?
faq.a: It explains what the symbols and colours on the map stand for.

faq.q: How can we find directions without a compass?
faq.a: The Sun rises in the east and sets in the west; at night the Pole Star shows the north.
